categories.main_business_segments: The company operates primarily in Internet Data Center (IDC) services and related internet comprehensive services. The main business segments include: (1) IDC services - providing server hosting, bandwidth rental, and IP address rental; (2) Internet comprehensive services - including content delivery network (CDN) acceleration, data synchronization, network security, and other value-added services; (3) Distributed photovoltaic energy services - investing in and operating distributed solar power generation projects; and (4) Optical communication equipment sales - selling optical modules and related products.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company's core technologies include Software Defined Network (SDN), automated operations and maintenance systems, and multi-network aggregation acceleration platforms. Key production methods involve: (1) self-built and leased standardized telecom-grade data centers with professional technical infrastructure; (2) multi-network service platforms connecting different basic telecom operators' networks; (3) cloud-native technology stack for distributed caching and disaster recovery; and (4) distributed photovoltaic power generation systems with intelligent energy management platforms for low-carbon data center operations.
categories.primary_customers_markets: The company primarily serves large and medium-sized internet enterprises and technology companies. Key customer industries include short video platforms, online gaming, live streaming, portal websites, e-commerce, and emerging AI/machine learning sectors. The company serves customers across multiple regions in China, with major customer concentration in internet and technology sectors. The top five customers account for 56.44% of annual sales revenue.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company operates across multiple regions in China with self-built data centers in key cities including: Beijing, Guangzhou, Shenzhen, Langfang, Tianjin, Chengdu, Haikou, Nanchang, and Nanning. The company has expanded to over 30 cities in China. Geographic segments include: South China region (30.68% of revenue), North China region (45.85% of revenue), other regions (11.36% of revenue), and Hong Kong/overseas markets (12.11% of revenue).
categories.supply_chain_position: The company operates in the midstream to downstream segments of the internet infrastructure supply chain. It is positioned downstream of basic telecom operators (China Telecom, China Unicom, China Mobile) from which it procures bandwidth and telecom resources. The company then provides IDC services and internet comprehensive services to downstream customers including internet enterprises, technology companies, and various industry clients requiring data center and cloud computing services.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: The company's strategic priorities include: (1) accelerating construction and delivery of major data center and intelligent computing center projects in key regions; (2) advancing carbon neutrality and new energy strategy through distributed photovoltaic projects; (3) developing core technologies in areas such as low-carbon intelligent computing center management platforms, multi-network aggregation acceleration platforms, unified disaster recovery platforms, and distributed caching platforms; (4) expanding AI and intelligent computing capabilities to support emerging applications; and (5) enhancing research and development investment with 89 R&D personnel and 3.08% of revenue allocated to R&D.
categories.revenue_model: The company generates revenue through multiple streams: (1) IDC services - monthly recurring revenue from machine cabinet rental, bandwidth rental, and IP address rental based on customer usage; (2) Internet comprehensive services - including CDN acceleration, data synchronization, network security services, and equipment sales with variable pricing; (3) Distributed photovoltaic energy services - revenue from selling generated electricity to customers at negotiated rates with monthly billing; and (4) System integration services - project-based revenue from data center construction and integration projects. Revenue is recognized upon service delivery or customer acceptance.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: The company is positioned as a leading professional IDC service provider in South China with significant presence in North China. It competes with other major IDC operators in China's competitive data center market. The company differentiates itself through: (1) extensive self-built data center infrastructure with over 43,000 standard cabinets; (2) strategic geographic positioning in tier-1 cities and key computing hubs; (3) multi-network connectivity with all major telecom operators; (4) advanced technical capabilities in SDN and automated operations; and (5) comprehensive service offerings combining IDC, cloud services, and emerging AI computing capabilities.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: The company is a mid-to-large scale technology infrastructure provider with significant growth trajectory. In 2024, the company achieved revenue of 2.165 billion yuan (62.18% increase from 2023), with net profit attributable to shareholders of 124.09 million yuan. Total assets reached 11.68 billion yuan (36.05% increase), and shareholders' equity was 3.34 billion yuan (9.05% increase). The company demonstrates strong operational cash flow of 715.03 million yuan. Growth is driven by expansion of data center capacity and increasing demand for AI computing infrastructure.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: The company's key value propositions include: (1) high-quality, stable, and secure internet infrastructure with multi-network connectivity ensuring service reliability; (2) strategic geographic positioning in key computing hubs aligned with national AI and digital infrastructure strategies; (3) comprehensive integrated solutions combining IDC services, cloud computing, and emerging AI computing capabilities; (4) commitment to green and low-carbon operations through carbon-neutral data centers and distributed renewable energy integration; (5) professional technical team with deep telecom and internet industry experience; and (6) scalable infrastructure supporting customers' growth from small to enterprise scale operations.
